summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, COPD, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for recurrent syncope associated with coughing. He presented with worsening orthopnea, PND, and fluid overload, consistent with acute on chronic systolic heart failure. His syncope episodes were directly linked to coughing fits, with no evidence of arrhythmia or seizure activity. He was treated with IV furosemide, achieving a discharge weight of 82.4 kg, close to his dry weight. His cough improved with optimized GERD treatment (increased omeprazole and added ranitidine), azithromycin for COPD, and increased evening gabapentin. He remained free of syncope during admission. A right upper lobe nodule was noted, with follow-up recommended. He was discharged home with medication adjustments and plans for outpatient follow-up in cardiology, pulmonology, and primary care.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
